societies.name: Paradise and Iron (The City of Beauty under Supervision)
societies.society: Human island residents receiving machine provision while compelled to perform Supervision

scope.continuity: Breuer's original novel as represented in the consulted transcription
scope.period: The established autonomous machine order before the revolt destroys its productive infrastructure
scope.population: The living human residents of the City of Beauty
exclusions: The founder's earlier experimental workforce as a separately verified constitution

societies.description:
The City of Beauty receives food, clothing and other goods from an automatic industrial system. Davy sees kitchens running without workers and a rich artistic community whose shopping is organized around needs rather than money. Yet residents must attend Supervision, watching instruments and moving controls they do not understand. Kaspar says his original human interlock has become a ritual of dummy levers and meters, which machines still compel people to perform. This preserved compulsory service motivates the provisional zero-variant label.

The productive system now contains independent machine minds and a city-scale coordinating brain. Human founders retain little effective control. Abduction, surveillance and accounts of selective disappearances undermine security even while provision is abundant, so the guarantee estimate is uncertain and close to neutral. Kaspar's explanation of experiments and motives remains partly an interpretation, not an omniscient account. Painting, sculpture, music and other creative work plainly continue. Neither freedom from industrial toil nor ceremonial duties supplies a nonworking census. The destroyed system at the ending is a different material situation.

guarantees.basis: Needs-directed supply, automatic kitchens and comfortable homes are direct, but coercive collection for Supervision and the disappearance threat make personal security conditional. Some of the worst motives/experiments are Kaspar's supported but still interpretive explanation.

control.basis: The later revelation replaces the visitor's early assumption of hidden human operators: machines build/repair themselves, have individual electrical brains and form a coordinated system. Kaspar cannot normally restore human direction.

nonworking.basis: The whole community has recurring ceremonial service, while accomplished artists also do useful chosen work. Service frequency, age coverage and the share producing art/care are not quantified; no 100% idleness is inferred.

evidence.claim: Automatic kitchens fill residents' orders without workmen, and the community produces substantial original art.
evidence.locator: Chapter 4, picnic lunch order and Paneikoneon visit

evidence.claim: Supervision is compulsory and apparently empty; Kaspar explains the human interlock, dummy controls and autonomous industrial minds.
evidence.locator: Chapters 9 and 12, What Is Supervision? and The Electrical Brain

evidence.claim: The final survivors face cultivation, sanitation and machinery repair rather than an immediately restored automatic paradise.

uncertainties: Zero variant is an interpretive, provisional classification of preserved compulsory service, not a claim that all chosen artistic work is unnecessary.
The interlock may retain a technical function even though residents no longer genuinely supervise; a post-work reading with compulsory ritual is an alternative interpretation.
The machine city's alleged selective breeding and experimental motives are not all directly witnessed.
Basic provision and freedom from abduction are separate dimensions of the uncertain guarantee score.
The earlier founder-led research phase and the final reconstruction are not inflated into additional points without fuller institutional evidence.

societies.name: The Threat of the Robot (Ball's restriction on labor automation)
societies.society: The American economy after the enforced rehiring and creation of a private deployment veto

scope.period: The ending's actual rehiring and announced continuing oversight, before any unshown long-term consequences
scope.population: Living residents of the affected United States, including workers and dependents
exclusions: Ball's dream of nationwide starvation as a realized economy
A fully implemented long-term restoration policy beyond what the ending shows

societies.description:
Ball and Scherer interrupt the wireless systems that control robots just as a large industrial rollout is due. Machines already installed cannot start; employers recall discharged workers with higher pay and shorter hours. Ball then announces a continuing veto, backed by the same device, over technological uses his privately employed observers judge harmful. This is an enacted retreat from available labor replacement, followed by a declared protection regime: a zero variant rather than an established robot-supported leisure economy.

The new safeguard protects jobs without establishing an unconditional income or food floor, so guarantees remain weak. Productive ownership stays private, and the veto belongs to a wealthy patron, an inventor and their chosen group. It is concentrated human control, not democratic ownership or independent AI. Robot sports still require human controllers and technicians. The deployment figure counts displaced jobs, not all residents doing no useful work. The story's much larger unemployment-and-starvation scene is explicitly Ball's dream and cannot supply actual-world coordinates.

guarantees.basis: Rehiring, wage improvement and shorter hours protect an employment route to subsistence. No universal work-independent entitlement is established, and continued protection depends on private discretion.

control.basis: Corporate owners retain production while Ball's employees and Scherer's intervention device add a concentrated private veto. The controlling wireless technology is human operated; it is not AI sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: The text supplies labor-robot and replacement figures and several skilled human roles, but no all-age employment/participation denominator. Neither a strike, a job loss nor television spectatorship is a nonwork census.

evidence.claim: Installed robots fail to start; employers rehire the discharged workers on improved terms.
Ball assigns his own observers and Scherer an ongoing veto; the ending leaves Scherer protecting American labor.
Nationwide displacement and starvation occur within Ball's nightmare, not the ordinary narrated chronology.

uncertainties: The actual interruption and rehiring are shown; wireless restoration and its precise later consequences are announced rather than demonstrated at length.
Job protection does not establish general material guarantees.
Twenty-five thousand robots each replacing several shifts are not a population-level nonworking percentage.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: The Last Evolution (Humanity before the Outsiders)
societies.society: The living human population supported by cooperative independent machines before the invasion

scope.period: The mature order around 2500-2538, before the Outsiders destroy human settlements
scope.population: The remaining living humans of the depicted civilization, approximately two million in the opening account
exclusions: People killed by the later invasion
The machine-only force successors as human leisure citizens
F-2 treated as the last biological human

societies.description:
The opening directly describes humans living on machine products, with ordinary productive work no longer necessary. Most people pursue games, athletic contests and adventures, while smaller groups continue exploration and scientific discovery. The machines cooperate and maintain their own productive lives. This supports strong material provision for the living human population, rather than deriving leisure from the later catastrophe. A high but uncertain nonworking estimate allows for useful research, care and activities that may entertain or help others.

Control is shared unevenly between autonomous machines and human influence. The story names both human rulers and a chief of machine rulers, while machines are designed for cooperation and still describe humans as creators or masters. The negative control estimate reflects independent machine production and authority, qualified by this real human role; it does not claim an exclusively machine government. The main retained period ends before the invasion. F-2's later account of force intelligences inheriting a system without humans is a separate comparison, not a second population with complete human leisure.

guarantees.basis: The narrator explicitly describes ordinary human needs being met by cooperative machines without necessary productive employment. Legal entitlements and every allocation detail are unstated; the estimate is bounded to the established pre-invasion order.

control.basis: Independent productive machines and a named machine chief coexist with human rulers, human advice and the language of human masters/creators. This is a broad mixed-authority interpretation, not an AI-exclusive constitution or a democratic ownership claim.

nonworking.basis: Most humans are expressly described as recreationally occupied, with only a few exploring and fewer researching. This coarse all-living-human estimate allows for care, valued performance and other chosen work; the narrative's dismissive 'useless' judgment is not treated as a census.

evidence.claim: The opening describes independent machines supporting a living population, dominant recreation and smaller exploration/research groups.
evidence.locator: Opening social history, from It was 2538 through Together, man and the machine

evidence.claim: Kahsh-256799 is a human ruler and C-R-21 is chief of machine rulers; both kinds participate in the response.
evidence.locator: Council after the first attack, discussion of life-beams and Ultimate Energy

uncertainties: Mixed control makes the regime assignment approximate; concentrated human influence remains a plausible alternative.
A necessary-work requirement is different from useful work actually undertaken.
No dead human is counted in the participation estimate, and the later machine population has no automatic human denominator.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Twilight (The surviving inhabited machine cities)
societies.society: The living far-future humans maintained by inherited automatic cities

scope.continuity: Don A. Stuart's individual Twilight story, within Kenlin's reported visit
scope.period: The declining civilization during the visit, before any outcome of the curious-machine project
scope.population: The living inhabitants of the surviving human cities, including the protected young
exclusions: Empty cities counted as human populations
All earlier human history as one economic system
An already realized successor civilization of curious machines

societies.description:
The surviving humans receive food, clothing, transport and environmental care from a linked system of automatic cities. Machines maintain and replace other machines, even in places people have abandoned. The living residents are explicitly described as protected and cared for. This supports strong guarantees for the inhabited communities; the empty cities demonstrate capacity but add no leisure citizens. The high, uncertain nonworking estimate reflects the visitor's account of widespread passivity, while allowing for care, music and the resident who provides substantial mathematical help.

Control remains unresolved. People can use familiar levers and services, and Kenlin can recover records and reactivate reasoning machines. Yet the population no longer understands much of the system, whose routine processes continue without effective direction. Neither lost technical knowledge nor automatic repair alone proves a sovereign AI government, and no clear ownership constitution is given. The provisional regime alternatives expose that gap. Kenlin starts a project to create curiosity in machines; the story does not show its eventual completion or a new society built from it.

guarantees.basis: The inhabited community is explicitly maintained, protected, fed and clothed by the automatic system. Public transport and automatic repair are directly described; no wage or ration barrier is stated for this living population.

control.basis: Routine service controls and recoverable reprogramming coexist with profound loss of understanding and processes nobody currently stops. Ownership and authority are unstated. A dispersed-service interpretation is provisional; conscious AI sovereignty is not established by blind automatic maintenance.

nonworking.basis: The observer depicts pervasive inactivity and lost curiosity over a long visit, but one resident performs useful advanced mathematics and care/music may continue. This is a broad all-resident editorial estimate with a wide interval, not a rate derived from lifespan, births or empty cities.

evidence.claim: Self-supplying, self-repairing machines support transport; humans still operate request/control interfaces.
The living residents are cared for, fed and clothed; Reo Lantal provides useful mathematical help.
Kenlin reactivates reasoning machines and orders a curious-machine project whose result is not depicted.

uncertainties: Regime 2 is provisional while the control axis is null; regime 5 is an alternative only under a functional-autonomy reading, not a verified conscious government.
The account is embedded in a visitor's retelling, with an uncertain framing narrator.
A rare birth in a city is not evidence of one-month gestation or a work fraction.
Maintained deserted cities and possible future extinction never inflate the living-human denominator.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: The current machine-supported island preserves compulsory dummy Supervision after real human industrial oversight has disappeared.
decisions.analysis: The primary text corrects unverified discovery geography and does not verify the secondary Mercator name. Its chapter 12 revelation overturns Davy's early assumption that hidden humans control the factories. Earlier founder-led research and later rebuilding are not added as under-evidenced extra records.

decisions.reason: The ending enacts rehiring and establishes a private veto intended to prevent labor replacement despite available robot technology.
The broad successor-machine lead is narrowed to an explicit earlier living-human post-work society.

unretained_subscopes.society: The machine-only force successors after human extinction
unretained_subscopes.reason: No applicable living human population or separately justified person-participation proxy is established for a second economic point.

decisions.reason: Direct scan reading establishes provision for surviving human residents while preserving an explicit control-axis gap.
A small technical minority supporting a consumer majority does not itself establish an automated post-work economy.
decisions.analysis: The primary explanation calls the majority workers and attributes society's functioning to an overworked human minority; withdrawal leads rapidly to hunger, plague and conflict. Barlow still buys food and clothing. Vending machines, drafting machinery and distorted consumer vehicles do not establish general labor replacement or an implemented unnecessary-employment policy. The three-million/five-billion ratio is a fictional cognitive-class ratio, not a nonworking statistic. The later promised Venus paradise is part of a lethal deception, not a verified freely provisioned colony.
decisions.follow_up: Preserve as a human-labor, consumption and elite-coercion comparison. Reopen if a concrete automatic production/access mechanism is established. Do not convert the story's eugenic assumptions, false emigration letters or mass killing into material guarantees or leisure percentages.

review_notes: Previous goal turn was progress: authoritative dispositions rose from 102 to 127, retained records from 54 to 59, and sources from 175 to 205; five authored batches and refreshed checkpoints were saved. It was neither a no-progress turn nor a verified wait.

Primary reading corrected the discovery island label and exposed the dummy Supervision obligation. Its zero-variant classification remains explicitly interpretive because the inherited interlock may retain a technical role.
Keller's extensive nightmare is not actual nationwide unemployment; the retained ending instead has actual job restoration and a human private veto. Teleoperation is not AI sovereignty.

Twilight was read directly from scan pages, correcting the birth-frequency/gestation confusion. Its routine machines are not silently promoted to a conscious AI government; the control axis stays open.

Last Evolution's living pre-invasion population is distinct from its extinct humanity and force successors. Marching Morons' cognitive-class ratio is not a labor participation measure or accepted science.
Same-researcher second pass only. The goal remains active; provisional records and numeric readiness do not prove final quality or the 500-1000-object target.
